params.name: a2
params.choice: [x for x in range(-8, 9) if abs(x) >= 2 and gcd(abs(x), q) == 1]

params.require: abs(a1) >= 2 and abs(a1) <= 12 and abs(a3) >= 2 and abs(a3) <= 12
params.why: the coefficients of k print as ak with no special cases and are not large

params.require: e3 != 0 and e3 != e2 and abs(e3) <= 14
params.why: no constant is 0, no difference of constants is 0, and nothing is large
the common difference is a proper fraction, so 'write it as a simplified fraction' is always accurate

constraints: d1 * k / q + f1 == d2 * k / q + f2
stem: If the following terms make a linear sequence: $\frac{{=a1}k}{{=q}} {=signed(e1)}\;;\;\frac{{=a2}k}{{=q}} {=signed(e2)}\;;\;\frac{{=a3}k}{{=q}} {=signed(e3)}\;;\;\ldots$ determine the value of $k$ and hence the numeric value of the common difference of the sequence. Write your answer as a simplified fraction.
solution: In a linear sequence the common difference is the same all the way along, so $T_{2} - T_{1} = T_{3} - T_{2}$.
Multiply every term by ${=q}$ to clear the fractions: $({=a2}k {=signed(q * e2)}) - ({=a1}k {=signed(q * e1)}) = ({=a3}k {=signed(q * e3)}) - ({=a2}k {=signed(q * e2)})$.
Collect the terms in $k$ on one side and the numbers on the other: ${=d1 - d2}k = {=q * (f2 - f1)}$.
Divide both sides by ${=d1 - d2}$: $k = \frac{{=q * (f2 - f1)}}{{=d1 - d2}} = {=k}$.

Now put $k = {=k}$ into the terms: $T_{1} = {=a1 / q} \times \left({=k}\right) {=signed(e1)} = {=v1}$, $T_{2} = {=a2 / q} \times \left({=k}\right) {=signed(e2)} = {=v2}$ and $T_{3} = {=a3 / q} \times \left({=k}\right) {=signed(e3)} = {=v3}$.
The common difference is $d = T_{2} - T_{1} = \left({=v2}\right) - \left({=v1}\right) = {=d}$. Check: $T_{3} - T_{2} = \left({=v3}\right) - \left({=v2}\right) = {=d}$, which is the same.
notes: Book ex3-1-16a / 16b: terms with fractional coefficients of k, found by T2 - T1 = T3 - T2 after multiplying through by the denominator, then the unknown is put back in (the book's 16b 'now determine the numeric value of the terms'). Two steps: solve for k, then evaluate the common difference d = T2 - T1 numerically. The family is built backwards: e3 = 2*e2 - e1 - w for a small non-zero whole number w, which makes k = q*w/A (A = d2 - d1 is never 0), so the equation has exactly one solution. The answer asked for is d = d1*w/A + (e2 - e1), always a non-zero proper fraction with denominator at most 4 (the require clause rejects whole-number d, so 'simplified fraction' in the stem is always accurate); because d is never a whole number, k never is either, as in the book (k = -5/3). The coefficients of k step by multiples of q (d1 = q*t1, d2 = q*t2), exactly as in the book's 16a where they step by -6 and 3 over denominator 3; so every a_i has the same remainder mod q as a2, and a2 is drawn coprime to q, which makes each printed fraction a_i*k/q already be in lowest terms. All coefficients in the terms have size 2 to 12 (never 0 or +-1), and the coefficients in the working (d1, d2, d1 - d2) have size at least 2 because q >= 2. Marker answer is built from numerator(d) and denominator(d) so it is plain maths, not LaTeX.
